sections.overview: Apistogramma gibbiceps is a dwarf cichlid recorded from Brazil’s middle Rio Negro and Rio Branco basins, where its populations occupy more than one water type.
sections.identification: The body is laterally compressed and becomes deeper with age; a dark stripe runs from the snout through the eye to the tail base, and older males may develop a rounded forehead hump. FishBase gives maximum standard lengths of 4.5 cm for male or unsexed fish and 5 cm for females; no reliable weight or body-width measurements were found. German and French aquarium accounts report about 8 cm for males and 5 cm for females without specifying the measurement convention, so these values should not be compared directly with standard length.
sections.habitat: Its range spans the middle Rio Negro and Rio Branco drainages; German species accounts describe shallow upper-river margins among roots and leaf litter, in soft, acidic water, and report both blackwater and clearer-water settings.
sections.diet: No species-specific stomach study was found; a recent aquarium synthesis infers from close Apistogramma relatives that it hunts small invertebrates in leaf litter and substrate, rather than presenting a measured diet for this fish.
sections.behavior: The available species account records female-led care of eggs and larvae, but detailed field observations of social behavior remain scarce.
sections.reproduction: It is a cave-spawning substrate brooder: the female attaches eggs to the cave ceiling and tends them and the larvae; FishBase cites one captive pair producing around 250 eggs every six weeks, not a typical wild clutch estimate.
sections.ecology: Apistogramma roraimae, described from the Rio Branco, is treated as a junior synonym of A. gibbiceps in current taxonomic catalogs, so older records under that name refer to this accepted species.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment is Least Concern, dated 7 November 2018; this broad category does not establish that every local habitat is unaffected by change.
